key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin combining thermal simulation and Gaussian-process surrogates shows promise for screening robotic welding conditions and control strategies before in-space joining experiments.
engineering_relevance: Fast surrogate predictions could support adaptive weld control when robot travel speed changes, helping maintain target weld geometry.
method: Finite-volume thermal model with phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and local pressure; gravity assessed separately.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates evaluated with repeated five-fold cross-validation.
Simulated UR5 seam tracking with proportional adjustment of the power-source setting.
evidence_signal: The GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs; 74/80 held-out solver responses fell within nominal 90% predictive intervals, and finite-volume checks placed 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop points within the illustrative width band.
watch_item: Results are simulation-only; thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and robotic hardware-in-the-loop validation remain necessary.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
